headline: Global $1.8B commitment to generate AI-ready biological data for predictive models
summary: Biohub, the U.S. Department of Energy, NIH, Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs, and Meta are investing in a massive international effort to create open, AI-ready biological datasets.
details: A global coalition, including Biohub, the U.S. Department of Energy, and the National Institutes of Health, has announced a $1.8 billion commitment. This funding, data, computation, and new measurement technology will generate AI-ready biological data, marking the largest coordinated effort to date.

The initiative aims to create an open resource for the research community, providing a foundation for understanding and treating human diseases. The Department of Energy will invest over $500 million over five years in lab measurement, modeling, and computation.

NIH will coordinate over $500 million in existing federal datasets and knowledge bases, working with Biohub to standardize them for AI model training. Additionally, Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs, and Meta are collectively investing $300 million in the Virtual Biology Initiative.

These datasets are designed to empower the global scientific community to build and utilize AI models. Researchers will be able to digitally ask, predict, and answer biological questions, accelerating the development of new disease prevention and treatment methods.

Alex Rives, Biohub Head of Science, stated that an accurate predictive model of biology could dramatically accelerate scientific discovery. This could unlock a greater understanding of disease and open new paths for cures, making the creation of a virtual cell a critical challenge.

The Virtual Biology Initiative, first announced in April 2026, coordinates data generation across institutions to build these AI-ready open datasets. Biohub's foundational $500 million commitment supports new technologies for measuring biological processes at unprecedented scale and detail.

Max Jaderberg, President of Isomorphic Labs, emphasized that solving predictive systems biology requires scaling beyond any single organization's current capabilities. Joining the Virtual Biology Initiative helps build a massive, multimodal data foundation for future breakthroughs.

Through its Genesis Mission, the Department of Energy will contribute over $500 million over five years to fundamental cell research. This includes data collection, AI analytics, measurement, imaging, modeling, and computation, leveraging exascale supercomputing and advanced microscopy.
